findings.title: Missing security header: Content-Security-Policy
findings.impact: Missing security headers reduce defense-in-depth against clickjacking, MIME-sniffing, and content-injection attacks; impact depends on which header is missing and what else the application does to compensate.
findings.remediation: Set Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Strict-Transport-Security, and Referrer-Policy appropriately for the application; avoid disclosing server/framework versions in Server/X-Powered-By headers.

findings.title: POST form has no anti-CSRF token field

metadata.note: absence of a token field name is suggestive, not proof (token could be delivered via header or double-submit cookie instead)

findings.impact: Allows tricking an authenticated victim's browser into submitting a state-changing request without their knowledge or consent.
findings.remediation: Use anti-CSRF tokens tied to the user's session for every state-changing form, and set cookies with SameSite=Lax or Strict.
